title: Linux creator has a simple message for AI holdouts: Fork off
excerpt: Linus Torvalds says Linux developers should embrace AI coding tools or fork the project, ending a heated open-source debate.
content_html:
Don't like AI? Linux's creator says go fork yourself

By Alistair Barr

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Author of the Tech Memo newsletter

I always assumed software engineers were naturally curious people who couldn't wait to try the latest technology. Lately, I'm realizing that's not always true.

I recently asked a developer friend whether she'd tried Claude Code or Codex, even for a few minutes over a weekend.

"Nope," she said proudly. This is a highly educated, experienced software engineer who works on big long-term projects.

Some techies, it turns out, are just as resistant to change as everyone else.

It's not just her. This is happening inside one of the most important software projects on earth.

Linux is the operating system that powers much of the internet, from cloud computing to smartphones and countless business systems.

It's also a huge open-source project, built by thousands of volunteers. Some of these developers want limits on using AI to write and review code.

Linus Torvalds, the creator of Linux, shut that down hard recently. AI, he argued, is simply another tool, which has gotten very good at writing and checking code and finding software bugs.

If folks don't want to use AI, they can go fork themselves, Torvalds quipped. (I'm here for the open-source dad jokes. A fork is when someone copies an existing piece of software and starts developing it separately as their own version).

"This is NOT some kind of 'social warrior' project, never has been, and never will be," Torvalds wrote on a Linux mailing list. "We make decisions primarily based on technical merit. Not fear of new tools."

A year ago, it was unclear whether AI would be this useful, but that's no longer in question, he said.

Torvalds admitted that AI can be "painful" to use sometimes, partly because it keeps finding bugs in software code written by humans, which can be embarrassing for software engineers.

"But the solution is not to put your head in the sand and sing 'La La
La, I can't hear you' at the top of your voice like some people seem
to do," he wrote.

content_html_zh:
不喜欢人工智能？ Linux 的创造者说自己去 fork

作者：Alistair Barr 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。 《技术备忘录》时事通讯的作者

我一直认为软件工程师天生好奇，迫不及待地想尝试最新技术。 最近，我意识到这并不总是正确的。

我最近问一位开发人员朋友，她是否尝试过 Claude Code 或 Codex，哪怕是在周末尝试过几分钟。

“不，”她自豪地说。 这是一位受过高等教育、经验丰富的软件工程师，从事大型长期项目。

事实证明，一些技术人员和其他人一样抵制变革。

不只是她。 这发生在地球上最重要的软件项目之一内。

Linux 是为互联网的大部分内容提供支持的操作系统，从云计算到智能手机以及无数的业务系统。

这也是一个巨大的开源项目，由数千名志愿者构建。 其中一些开发人员希望限制使用人工智能编写和审查代码。

Linux 的创建者 Linus Torvalds 最近大力关闭了它。 他认为，人工智能只是另一种工具，它非常擅长编写和检查代码以及发现软件错误。

托瓦尔兹打趣道，如果人们不想使用人工智能，他们可以自己分叉。 （我来这里是为了听开源老爸笑话。 分叉是指有人复制现有软件并开始将其单独开发为自己的版本）。

“这不是某种‘社会战士’项目，过去不是，也永远不会是，”Torvalds 在 Linux 邮件列表中写道。 “我们主要根据技术优势做出决定。 不惧怕新工具。”

他说，一年前，人们还不清楚人工智能是否会如此有用，但现在已经不再是问题了。

Torvalds 承认，人工智能有时使用起来会“痛苦”，部分原因是它不断在人类编写的软件代码中发现错误，这可能会让软件工程师感到尴尬。

“但解决办法不是像有些人那样把头埋在沙子里，用最高的声音唱‘拉拉拉，我听不到你’，”他写道。
